correctedCritiques.pro-coherentist-web-no-arbitrary-stop: Strongest feature: The reply frames justification as a coherentist web and presses why primitive logic may terminate explanation while primitive theology may not. Principal limitation: Calling that terminus arbitrary does not establish arbitrariness, since primitive logical necessity may have comparative advantages unavailable to an equally primitive divine posit. Live burden: The affirmative must supply nonquestion-begging criteria for acceptable termini, apply them symmetrically to logic and God, and address fallibilist, proportioned confidence instead of treating every unexplained primitive as unrestricted ad hoc assertion. Locked score: The mixed band reflects contact with the primitive-logic defense and coherentist perspective, reduced by responsiveness, implicit nonarbitrariness standards, weakened treatment of the strongest alternative, and the overstated contention that arbitrariness ends rational debate.
correctedCritiques.con-reductio-must-exhaust-alternatives: Strongest feature: The reply identifies two indispensable bridges in the necessity argument: showing that the phenomenon needs explanation and that relevant competing explanations fail before theism follows. Principal limitation: Demanding elimination of every logically possible alternative would be excessive, though the locked formulation confines the requirement to relevant live alternatives within the transcendental reductio. Live burden: The affirmative must meet those requirements or show that denying the Orthodox ground produces contradiction, while the negative must allow class-level exclusion without enumerating limitless imaginative possibilities. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional precision, responsiveness, calibration, and motion-level relevance, qualified only by how comprehensively alternatives must be surveyed and whether a formulated transcendental strategy could exclude them collectively.
